title: Portuguese explorer Pedro de Sintra names Sierra Leone
description: Portuguese navigator Pedro de Sintra mapped the coast and named the mountainous peninsula Serra Lyoa (Lion Mountains), origin of the country's name.

title: Founding of the Province of Freedom
description: British abolitionists settled freed slaves at Granville Town, an early settlement that preceded the colony for liberated Africans.

title: Freetown founded by Nova Scotian settlers
description: Freed black Loyalists from Nova Scotia established Freetown, which became the capital and a haven for liberated Africans.

title: Sierra Leone becomes a British Crown Colony
description: Britain took over the settlement, making Freetown a base for the Royal Navy's anti-slavery patrols off West Africa.

title: Sierra Leone gains independence from Britain
description: On 27 April 1961 Sierra Leone became an independent nation within the Commonwealth, with Milton Margai as its first prime minister.

title: Outbreak of the Sierra Leone Civil War
description: The Revolutionary United Front launched a rebellion that triggered an eleven-year civil war notorious for the use of blood diamonds and child soldiers.

title: End of the civil war
description: The brutal conflict was declared over after UN and British intervention, beginning a long process of reconstruction and reconciliation.

title: Ebola epidemic strikes Sierra Leone
description: The West African Ebola outbreak devastated the country, killing thousands before being contained by 2016.

title: Land of Punt trades with ancient Egypt
description: The Horn of Africa region, often linked with the fabled Land of Punt, supplied incense, gold and ivory to ancient Egyptian expeditions.

title: Rise of Mogadishu as a trading hub
description: Mogadishu grew into a wealthy Indian Ocean port, trading gold and goods with Arabia, Persia, India and beyond.

title: Adal Sultanate fights Ethiopia
description: The Muslim Adal Sultanate, centered in the Horn, waged prolonged wars with the Christian Ethiopian Empire.

title: Sultanate of the Geledi and colonial pressures
description: Local Somali sultanates flourished even as European and Egyptian powers began to encroach on the Somali coast.

title: Dervish movement led by Sayyid Mohammed Abdullah Hassan
description: The Dervish State resisted British, Italian and Ethiopian colonization for two decades in a major anti-colonial struggle.

title: Somalia gains independence and unifies
description: British Somaliland and Italian Somaliland merged on 1 July 1960 to form the independent Somali Republic.

title: Collapse of the Siad Barre government
description: The fall of dictator Siad Barre plunged Somalia into civil war and prolonged statelessness.

title: Federal Government of Somalia established
description: Somalia adopted a provisional constitution and formed its first permanent central government since 1991.

title: Early modern humans at the southern coast
description: Sites such as Blombos Cave preserve some of the earliest evidence of symbolic behavior and tool use by Homo sapiens.

title: Bartolomeu Dias rounds the Cape of Good Hope
description: The Portuguese navigator became the first European to sail around the southern tip of Africa, opening a sea route to Asia.

title: Dutch establish Cape Town
description: Jan van Riebeeck founded a Dutch East India Company resupply station at the Cape, beginning permanent European settlement.

title: Anglo-Zulu War
description: The Zulu Kingdom fought Britain, winning a famous victory at Isandlwana before ultimately being defeated.

title: Union of South Africa formed
description: Four British colonies united to create the self-governing Union of South Africa within the British Empire.

title: Apartheid system introduced
description: The National Party institutionalized apartheid, a legal system of racial segregation and white minority rule.

title: First democratic elections; Mandela elected president
description: Apartheid ended as all races voted freely, electing Nelson Mandela as South Africa's first black president.

title: South Africa hosts the FIFA World Cup
description: South Africa became the first African nation to host the football World Cup, a landmark moment for the continent.

title: Turco-Egyptian penetration of the south
description: Egyptian forces under Muhammad Ali pushed up the Nile, drawing the southern Sudan region into wider conquest and the slave trade.

title: Anglo-Egyptian Condominium over Sudan
description: Britain and Egypt jointly administered Sudan, including the south, often governing the region separately from the north.

title: First Sudanese Civil War begins
description: Southern soldiers mutinied at Torit, igniting a long conflict between the marginalized south and the Khartoum government.

title: Second Sudanese Civil War and the SPLA
description: John Garang founded the Sudan People's Liberation Army, launching a war that lasted over two decades.

title: Comprehensive Peace Agreement signed
description: The agreement ended the second civil war and granted the south autonomy with a path toward a self-determination referendum.

title: South Sudan becomes independent
description: Following an overwhelming referendum vote, South Sudan declared independence on 9 July 2011 as the world's newest nation.

title: Outbreak of the South Sudanese Civil War
description: Political rivalry between President Salva Kiir and Riek Machar erupted into a devastating civil war.

title: Kingdom of Kerma flourishes in Nubia
description: The Kerma civilization became one of Africa's earliest urban states, rivaling ancient Egypt along the Nile.

title: Kushite kings rule Egypt
description: The Kingdom of Kush, based at Napata, conquered Egypt and ruled as the 25th Dynasty of black pharaohs.

title: Meroe becomes capital of Kush
description: The Kushite kingdom shifted south to Meroe, famed for ironworking, pyramids and the Meroitic script.

title: Aksum sacks Meroe
description: The Ethiopian Kingdom of Aksum invaded, hastening the decline of the once-powerful Meroitic state.

title: Egyptian conquest founds Khartoum
description: Ottoman-Egyptian forces conquered northern Sudan and established Khartoum as an administrative center.

title: Mahdist forces capture Khartoum
description: The Mahdist uprising defeated Anglo-Egyptian forces and killed General Gordon, founding an independent Islamic state.

title: Sudan gains independence
description: Sudan became an independent republic on 1 January 1956, ending Anglo-Egyptian rule.

title: Revolution ousts Omar al-Bashir
description: Mass protests led the military to remove President Omar al-Bashir after three decades of authoritarian rule.

title: Portuguese discover uninhabited islands
description: Portuguese navigators reached the uninhabited islands of Sao Tome and Principe, claiming them for Portugal.

title: First permanent settlement on Sao Tome
description: Portugal began colonizing the islands, soon making them a major sugar producer using enslaved African labor.

title: Amador's slave rebellion
description: Enslaved Africans led by Amador rose in revolt and briefly controlled much of Sao Tome, a landmark resistance.

title: Cocoa and coffee plantations rise
description: In the 19th century the islands became leading cocoa producers, worked by contract laborers under harsh conditions.

title: Batepa massacre
description: Portuguese colonial authorities killed many Forros laborers in a brutal crackdown that fueled nationalist sentiment.

title: Sao Tome and Principe gains independence
description: The islands became an independent republic from Portugal on 12 July 1975 following the Carnation Revolution.

title: First multiparty elections held
description: Sao Tome and Principe transitioned from single-party socialist rule to multiparty democracy.

title: Early hominins at Olduvai Gorge
description: Olduvai Gorge and Laetoli preserve some of the oldest fossils and footprints of early human ancestors.

title: Swahili city-state of Kilwa flourishes
description: Kilwa Kisiwani became a wealthy Indian Ocean trade center exporting gold, ivory and goods across the region.

title: Vasco da Gama reaches the Swahili coast
description: The Portuguese explorer stopped at coastal cities en route to India, foreshadowing Portuguese dominance of the coast.

title: Sultan of Oman moves capital to Zanzibar
description: Said bin Sultan relocated his seat to Zanzibar, making it a center of the clove and slave trades.

title: Maji Maji Rebellion against German rule
description: A widespread uprising challenged German colonial control of Tanganyika before being violently suppressed.

title: Tanganyika gains independence
description: Tanganyika became independent from Britain on 9 December 1961 under Julius Nyerere.

title: Union forms the United Republic of Tanzania
description: Tanganyika and Zanzibar united to create Tanzania following the Zanzibar Revolution.

title: Arusha Declaration sets socialist course
description: Nyerere proclaimed ujamaa, a policy of African socialism and self-reliance that reshaped Tanzanian society.

title: Ewe and Mina peoples settle the region
description: Migrating Ewe and coastal Mina communities established the societies that form much of modern Togo's population.

title: Coastal area drawn into Atlantic slave trade
description: The Togo coast became part of the 'Slave Coast,' where European traders bought captives for the Americas.

title: Germany establishes Togoland protectorate
description: Germany signed treaties making Togoland a colony, which it developed as a model plantation territory.

title: Togoland falls to Allied forces
description: During World War I, British and French troops seized German Togoland, later dividing it under League of Nations mandates.

title: Togo gains independence
description: French Togoland became the independent Republic of Togo on 27 April 1960, with Sylvanus Olympio as leader.

title: Gnassingbe Eyadema seizes power
description: Eyadema took control in a coup and ruled Togo for 38 years, one of Africa's longest reigns.

title: Faure Gnassingbe succeeds his father
description: After Eyadema's death, his son Faure became president amid disputed elections and protests.

title: Founding of Carthage
description: Phoenician settlers from Tyre founded Carthage, which grew into a dominant Mediterranean maritime power.

title: Hannibal crosses the Alps
description: Carthaginian general Hannibal led an army with elephants over the Alps to invade Rome in the Second Punic War.

title: Rome destroys Carthage
description: Rome razed Carthage at the end of the Third Punic War, making the region the province of Africa.

title: Arabs found Kairouan
description: Arab conquerors established Kairouan, which became a major center of Islamic learning and the Great Mosque.

title: Tunisia becomes an Ottoman province
description: The Ottomans took control of Tunis, which later became a largely autonomous beylik.

title: France establishes a protectorate
description: France imposed a protectorate over Tunisia under the Treaty of Bardo, beginning colonial rule.

title: Tunisia gains independence
description: Tunisia became independent from France on 20 March 1956, with Habib Bourguiba leading the new nation.

title: Jasmine Revolution sparks the Arab Spring
description: Mass protests ousted President Ben Ali, igniting uprisings across the Arab world.

title: Kingdom of Bunyoro-Kitara rises
description: The powerful Bunyoro-Kitara kingdom dominated the Great Lakes region in the medieval period.

title: Buganda kingdom emerges
description: The Kingdom of Buganda grew into one of the most influential states in the Lake Victoria region.

title: John Hanning Speke reaches Buganda
description: The British explorer visited the court of Buganda while seeking the source of the Nile.

title: Uganda becomes a British protectorate
description: Britain declared a protectorate over the Buganda kingdom and surrounding territories.

title: Uganda gains independence
description: Uganda became independent from Britain on 9 October 1962, with Milton Obote as prime minister.

title: Idi Amin seizes power
description: Idi Amin took control in a coup and ruled brutally until 1979, expelling Asians and killing many Ugandans.

title: Yoweri Museveni takes power
description: Museveni's National Resistance Army captured Kampala, beginning his long presidency.

title: Trade and settlement on the central plateau
description: Iron-working Bantu-speaking communities engaged in copper and trade networks across what is now Zambia.

title: Livingstone reaches Victoria Falls
description: Explorer David Livingstone became the first European to view the falls on the Zambezi, naming them for Queen Victoria.

title: British South Africa Company administers the region
description: Cecil Rhodes's company gained control over the territory that became Northern Rhodesia.

title: Copperbelt mining boom begins
description: Large-scale copper mining transformed the economy and society of Northern Rhodesia.

title: Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland formed
description: Northern Rhodesia was joined into a federation, a move that fueled African nationalist opposition.

title: Zambia gains independence
description: Northern Rhodesia became the Republic of Zambia on 24 October 1964, with Kenneth Kaunda as first president.

title: Multiparty democracy returns
description: Frederick Chiluba defeated Kaunda in elections, ending single-party rule peacefully.

title: Great Zimbabwe rises
description: The stone city of Great Zimbabwe became the capital of a powerful kingdom that controlled regional gold trade.

title: Kingdom of Mutapa emerges
description: As Great Zimbabwe declined, the Mutapa Empire rose to dominate trade between the interior and the coast.

title: Ndebele kingdom established
description: Mzilikazi led the Ndebele people into the region, founding a kingdom centered near present-day Bulawayo.

title: Pioneer Column establishes colonial rule
description: Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company occupied the territory, which became Southern Rhodesia.

title: First Chimurenga uprising
description: The Shona and Ndebele rose against British colonial rule in a major anti-colonial rebellion.

title: Rhodesia's Unilateral Declaration of Independence
description: The white minority government under Ian Smith declared independence from Britain to preserve minority rule.

title: Zimbabwe gains independence
description: After a long liberation war, Zimbabwe became independent on 18 April 1980, with Robert Mugabe as leader.

title: Mugabe resigns after military intervention
description: Robert Mugabe stepped down after 37 years in power following a military takeover and mass protests.
